BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r1.claim: The phrase “when their brother said to them” is a temporal clause attached to the account of denial; brotherhood is by lineage.
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r1.anchor: {إذ قال لهم أخوهم} في النسب ظرف للتكذيب.

BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r2.claim: Some say Hūd’s original name was ʿĀbir, he was called Hūd for dignity and calmness, lived 150 years, and was sent to ʿĀd at forty.
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : كان اسم هود عابرا وسمي هودا لوقاره وسكونه عاش مائة وخمسين سنة أرسل إلى أورد عاد حين بلغ الأربعين

BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r3.claim: Hūd asks whether they will not fear God and stop their conduct, especially associating partners and risking divine punishment.
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r3.anchor: الله تعالى فتفعلون ما تفعلون : وبالفارسية (آيا رهيز نميكنيد از شرك واز عقاب إلهي خائف نمي شويد).

STUDYQURAN:26:123/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:123/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:123/r1.claim: The five opening verses of Hūd's story follow the same pattern as Noah's and the stories of later prophets.
STUDYQURAN:26:123/r1.anchor: These five verses form a pattern that opens the story of Noah and each of the prophets who follow

TAB-FULL:v17p606#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p606#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p606#2/r1.claim: ʿĀd denied God’s messengers when Hūd, their brother, urged them to fear God’s punishment for disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v17p606#2/r1.anchor: الله على كفركم به. {إني لكم رسول} [الشعراء: 107] من ربي

TABATABAI:26:123-130/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r1.claim: The story concerns Hud and ʿAd; as in Noah's story, the people are called deniers of the messengers although they outwardly rejected only one.
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r1.anchor: بيان تشير الآيات إلى قصة هود عليه السلام وقومه وهم قوم عاد

TABATABAI:26:123-130/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r5.claim: Some exegetes say these stories stress that the prophets are trustworthy, seek no wage, and command piety and obedience to show their shared mission of true knowledge and conduct leading to reward and away from punishment, despite differences in detailed laws across eras.
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن تصدير هذه القصص الخمس بذكر أمانة الرسل وعدم سؤالهم أجرا

TABRISI:26:123-128/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:123-128/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:123-128/r16.claim: Hud is their brother by lineage.
TABRISI:26:123-128/r16.anchor: إذ قال لهم أخوهم } في النسب { هود ألا تتقون

TABRISI:26:123-128/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:123-128/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:123-128/r17.claim: Hud calls them to fear God by avoiding disobedience.
TABRISI:26:123-128/r17.anchor: هود ألا تتقون } الله باجتناب معاصيه

ELMALILI:26:123-140/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:123-140/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:123-140/r1.claim: Hūd asks his people whether they will not fear God.
ELMALILI:26:123-140/r1.anchor: O vakit ki kardeşleri Hûd onlara demişti: “Siz Allah’tan korkmaz mısınız? (124).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:124/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:124/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:124/r1.claim: The commentary renders Hud’s question as asking whether his people are not avoiding disobedience to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:124/r1.anchor: Kardeşleri Hûd onlara şöyle demişti: “Allah’a karşı gelmekten sakınmıyor musunuz

ASAD-NOTES:26:123#n55/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:123#n55/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:123#n55/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to the account of Hud and ʿAd at 7:65 and its note 48.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p220/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p220/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p220/r1.claim: Across these occurrences, buʿd is the opposite of nearness, while naʾy specifically means turning away and refusing, the opposite of turning toward.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p220/r1.anchor: والبعد، فيها جميعاً، نقيض القرب على حين يخلص النأي للصد والإعراض، نقيض الإقبال.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.claim: Samarrāʾī distinguishes Midian from the Aykah people: Shuaib belonged to Midian, so he is called their brother when addressing Midian but not Aykah; the other Shuʿara prophets address their own peoples.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.anchor: ومدين غير أصحاب الأيكة، وشعيب عليه السلام كان من مدين ولم يكن من أصحاب الأيكة ولذلك إذا ذكرت مدين قال: (أخوهم)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p430/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p430/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p430/r3.claim: Where the previous sūrah detailed Moses and Noah but briefly mentioned intervening nations, this sūrah details those nations’ dealings with their messengers and their fates in historical order, ending each account with a refrain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p430/r3.anchor: The sequence adopted is historical and at the end of every anecdote the repetitive verses occur.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p431/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p431/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p431/r2.claim: Hud was their own brother, not a stranger; they knew his impeccable life, so treating him as a liar or fabricator reflects their utter misfortune.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p431/r2.anchor: The verse says that Hūd (sws) was their brother and not a stranger to them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p433/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p433/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p433/r1.claim: The recurring prophetic appeal is an earnest, affectionate final warning: the people still have time to abandon wrongdoing and follow their messenger rather than corrupt leaders.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p433/r1.anchor: These words serve to remind and caution the nation in a very earnest and affectionate way in the last phase.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p122/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p122/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p122/r7.claim: Hud is called their brother by lineage, not by religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p122/r7.anchor: إذ قال لهم أخوهم هود} يعني في النسب لا في الدين،

BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r6.claim: Hud was their known brother, whose sincerity, counsel, and fidelity they already knew; their failure to pause for reflection emphasizes the immediacy of their rejection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r6.anchor: وقد عرفوا صدق إخائه , وعظيم نصحه ووفائه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r7.claim: The particle alā introduces a gentle, courteous appeal, softening the exhortation so it might reach them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r7.anchor: ألا } بصيغة العرض تأدبا معهم وتلطفا بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r8.claim: Hud calls them to fear their Creator by worshipping Him alone and not associating anything powerless to harm or benefit.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r8.anchor: أي تكون منكم تقوى لربكم الذي خلقكم فتعبدوه وحده ولا تشركوا به ما لا يضر ولا ينفع

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2792#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2792#3/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2792#3/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says ʿĀd lived in Yemen at al-Ahqaf, the sand dunes; Hud admonished and reminded them of the Qur'anic account, but they denied him and demanded punishment.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2792#3/r1.anchor: السدي قال : ان عاد كانوا قوما باليمن بالاحقاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p164#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p164#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p164#2/r4.claim: The explanation of ألا تتقون is the same as in the parallel opening of Noah’s story.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p164#2/r4.anchor: مثل القول في نظيره المتقدم في قصة قوم نوح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p238#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p238#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p238#2/r2.claim: Hūd addresses them as the other messengers address their peoples.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p238#2/r2.anchor: وخاطبهم «هود» عليه السلام بمثل مخاطبة سائر الرسل

MUQATIL:26:123-131/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:123-131/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:123-131/r1.claim: Hud was their brother by lineage, not by religion.
MUQATIL:26:123-131/r1.anchor: ليس بأخيهم فى الدين ولكن أخوهم فى النسب

MUQATIL:26:123-131/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:123-131/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:123-131/r2.claim: “Will you not be God-conscious?” means “Will you not fear God?”
MUQATIL:26:123-131/r2.anchor: يعنى ألا تخشون الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:26:123-129/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:123-129/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:123-129/r3.claim: Hud’s call to fear God is explained as in the preceding account of Noah.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:123-129/r3.anchor: إذ قال لهم أخوهم هود ألا تتقون * إني لكم رسول أمين
